Resolves #18883

Related: #18762

🪢 *Scroll an open edit out of view, press Tab, and focus walked off with the draft still open. Now the draft commits and the next cell is edited — the grid scrolls back by itself.*

**`src/main/DomEvents.mjs`** — `registerPreventDefaultKeys({id, keys})` / `unregisterPreventDefaultKeys({id})`: the default of the named keys is cancelled while the registered node is the keydown target, and the event is still delivered to the App Worker. `registerDisabledInputChars` could not serve: it is gated on INPUT / TEXTAREA and swallows the key. An App Worker handler cannot cancel a default after dispatch, so the node is registered before the key arrives.

**`src/grid/plugin/CellEditing.mjs`**
- `setSession()` is now the single write to `session` (four sites), and holds the View's Tab for exactly as long as a session is open.
- `onTabKey` accepts the View as the key's source and runs the same terminal as the mounted path.
- `startEdit(record, dataField, allowSuspended)` — the next edit may start on a cell whose Row is not rendered: the editor is born with its body as stand-in parent, and the Row that renders the record takes it over (`grid.Row#applyRendererOutput` already re-parents on embed). The public default still refuses an unrendered cell.
- An invalid suspended draft scrolls its own cell back into sight and takes focus once embodied.
- The target row is now always asked into sight (`scrollByRows(index, 0)`), which the suspended case needs even for a same-row move.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium, real keys, CI-executed e2e tier) → L3 required (AC-1…AC-5). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the PR baseline jobs run in CI. Change class: capability (`feat`).

## Deltas from ticket

- **Registered for the session's lifetime, not only while suspended** (ticket revised). There is no event for "the embodiment went", and a session that is embodied but unfocused — what every reprojection leaves — has the same problem.
- **The end state cannot prove the registration.** The App Worker handles the Tab either way and the embodied editor focuses itself, so every arm passed with the registration removed. The focus trail is what reddens: uncancelled, focus first moves to a scrollbar or out of the grid and is pulled back — a bounce every ancestor sees as the grid losing focus.
- **"Tab leaves the grid" was the wrong criterion for the no-session arm:** the browser's traversal goes View → the grid's own scrollbars → out. The arm asserts that focus moves off the View, which a leaked registration prevents (S2).

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

Per §9 Strategic-Fit Step-Back:
- **Decision**: Approve
- **Rationale**: A registration that outlives its session would silently hijack Tab on that grid forever, so this change lives or dies on one invariant — every path that ends a session must unregister. It is enforced structurally (`setSession` is the single write, and I verified no assignment escaped it) and witnessed by an arm that checks both before any edit and after one ended. The main-thread addition mirrors its sibling exactly and is gated on a registered node id, so it cannot reach a grid that did not ask for it.

**Peer-Review Opening:** Funnelling every `session` write through `setSession()` is what turns "remember to unregister on four paths" into an invariant a grep can check. That is the difference between this being reviewable and being a leak waiting for the fifth path someone adds next month.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**The invariant, checked rather than trusted.** A stale `preventDefaultKeys` entry would cancel Tab on that View for the page's lifetime, so I enumerated every write to `session` at this head rather than reading the four converted sites and assuming they were all:

```
 81:  me.setSession(null)        cancelEdit
108:  me.setSession(null)        completeEdit
135:  me.setSession(null)        destroy, owner.isDestroying
441:  setSession(session) {      the definition
446:      me.session = session   the only assignment
516:  me.setSession({…})         startEdit
```

Nothing escaped. And arm 4 is the part I would have asked for if it were missing: it presses Tab on the View **before any edit** and **after one ended**, asserting focus leaves the View both times. A missing `unregisterPreventDefaultKeys` fails that second assertion — the arm witnesses the absence of the suppression, not just its presence, which is the only way to test a teardown.

**Non-blocking, one destroy-order edge.** `setSession` reads `let {view} = me.owner` and gates on `&& view`. `destroy()` two lines above shows `owner.view` can already be gone (`{keys} = owner.view || {}`), and when it is, the unregister is skipped and one `preventDefaultKeys[viewId]` entry persists for the page's life. I am **not** asking for a guard: the entry is keyed by a node id that no longer exists and Neo instance ids do not recur, so it is a bounded memory key per grid destroyed mid-edit, never a behaviour leak. Worth knowing it is there; not worth code to prevent something unobservable.

**§5.4, and why I am not raising a Required Action.** This mints a genuinely new consumed surface — `registerPreventDefaultKeys` / `unregisterPreventDefaultKeys` on the `remote.app` list, callable by any App-worker code — and neither #18883 nor the parent epic #18762 carries a Contract Ledger. I checked the precedent before deciding: the sibling this mirrors, `registerDisabledInputChars`, arrived in `4038f31f1b` (#4416) with none either, so demanding one for the third member of a family that has zero would be inconsistent rather than diligent. More to the point, the contract a ledger would carry here — who registers, who removes, and on which transitions — is written where it binds, in `setSession`'s docblock. If that family is ever documented properly, this is the PR that made it three.

**Also checked and clean:** the `onTabKey` source test widened to `owner.body.isEditorEvent(data) || data.path?.[0]?.id === view.id`, so a Tab on any *other* node inside the View keeps its default — the comment says so and the condition matches it. `startEdit`'s new `allowSuspended` only relaxes the `!row` bail, and the editor parents to `me.getBody(column)` until a Row takes it over, which is the same "born suspended" state `isEmbodied` already answers for.
